articles.summary: arXiv:2611.27186v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM simulations are validated by equivalence with human effects, yet a zero reference passes whenever the human 90 percent interval lies inside the margin, as the human benchmark shows before simulation. When the zero reference fails, planned precision gives independent simulations the margin up to which passing is a 5 percent test of response. articles.title: No Perfect Guardrail & No Perfect Guard: On the Decidability of Output Policies for Large Language Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.27260v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Expecting guardrails to provide a general guarantee of safety fails to recognize the limits of computational enforcement and policy specification. We argue that promising such perfection is an ethical failure of precision, and that invoking it to abdicate responsibility is a moral failure. Guardrails can support responsible action, but cannot relieve researchers, developers, policymakers, or users of their obligations to examine what they claim, permit, and prevent. articles.title: Standard-Anchored Delegation in Teachers' Use of Generative AI
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.27533v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Teachers who use generative AI must decide which parts of their work to hand over, while they remain accountable for what reaches students. We studied these decisions in Punjab, Pakistan, through a qualitatively driven mixed-methods study. We interviewed 13 teachers from government, private, NGO and vocational institutions, four administrators and one student, and coded each teacher's position on twelve educational tasks. articles.title: How coalition size shapes bill cosponsorship in the U.S. Congress
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.27565v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Legislation is built by coalitions, yet studied through pairwise ties. Using five decades of U.S. House and Senate cosponsorship (1973-2025), we represent each bill as a group. Prior ties to current members predict who joins better than ties to the sponsor, and group history (earlier co-appearance with pairs of those members) produces a larger likelihood gain than sponsor ties alone. articles.title: Synthetic Doubt and the Integrity of Digital Proof before the International Criminal Court
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21455v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence complicates evidentiary assessment at the International Criminal Court by enabling fabricated audiovisual material and making authentic digital evidence easier to dismiss as fake. articles.title: OpinionGPT: Modelling Explicit Biases in Instruction-Tuned LLMs
articles.summary: arXiv:2309.03876v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Instruction-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently showcased remarkable ability to generate fitting responses to natural language instructions. However, an open research question concerns the inherent biases of trained models and their responses. For instance, if the data used to tune an LLM is dominantly written by persons with a specific political bias, we might expect generated answers to share this bias. articles.summary: arXiv:2508.16662v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) has become a widely adopted model for securing enterprise environments, promoting continuous verification and minimal trust across systems. articles.summary: arXiv:2510.04392v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems are increasingly deployed in high-stakes domains where users expect outputs to be consistent across semantically equivalent queries.
